title: Sovereign AI Control Plane Backlog
invariants: Starlight creates the trace_id before provider dispatch.
Trace/span correlation uses Starlight-owned OpenTelemetry/W3C-compatible identifiers; vendor identifiers remain shadow references.
Secret records never leave local authority.
Regulated records require an explicit external-mirror policy.
A provider trace ID is a shadow reference, not the canonical receipt.
Provider failure cannot prevent the local trace receipt.
Production feedback becomes a candidate evaluation case, never automatic truth.
No per-terminal heavyweight collector, index, or memory runtime.

work_items.title: Define the provider-neutral, OpenTelemetry-compatible ControlPlaneTraceEnvelope and pure builder
work_items.why: Provides one immutable correlation and policy shape across direct providers, optional gateways, agent runs, tool calls, and evaluations without introducing a runtime dependency.
dependencies: Clean dedicated worktree based on the intended starlight-memory commit
acceptance: Types compile.
A pure buildMemoryAddTrace(record, policy, context) uses existing routeMemoryRecord and estimateProviderResourcePlan primitives.
Fixtures prove a 32-hex trace ID, 16-hex span and parent-span IDs, and Starlight-owned project, thread, and session correlation across an agent, tool, and model span.
A duplicate terminal write with the same event_id or idempotency_key does not create a second receipt.
Tests first prove parent-child spans, unknown cost, privacy classes, prompt references, and provider shadow references.
Serialized output contains no raw memory content, prompt text, tokens, secrets, absolute filesystem paths, display names, or email addresses.
No runtime dependency is added.
work_items.risk: Do not let a generic trace schema become a second policy system or turn external identity fields into canonical identities; reference existing SIS privacy and provenance types.

work_items.title: Write durable local trace receipts with bounded indexing
work_items.why: Closes the core observability gap while retaining local sovereignty and operation during vendor outage.
acceptance: Write succeeds before optional provider export.
Trace lookup by trace_id works after process restart.
Disk and retention behavior is explicit and bounded.
Provider dispatch failure still creates a failed trace receipt.
work_items.risk: No new per-agent daemon or unbounded local payload retention.

work_items.title: Add policy-aware trace export decisions
work_items.why: Makes OpenTelemetry and optional vendor export safe without treating the vendor as canonical.
acceptance: Secret traces are local-only.
Regulated traces default local-only.
Redacted export has a provenance receipt.
Export is skipped, not retried blindly, when policy denies it.
work_items.risk: Input/output payloads must not leak under metadata or error fields.

work_items.title: Create trace-to-evaluation candidate selection and typed human review
work_items.why: Turns production failures and corrections into measurable regression cases rather than dashboard noise, while keeping a correction distinct from an accepted fixture.
acceptance: Feedback, policy blocks, and configured failures create de-duplicated candidate cases.
Candidate has trace, prompt, evaluator, and privacy provenance.
Review schemas validate categorical, range, and correction annotations without retaining raw secret payloads.
Candidate promotion requires independent evaluation evidence and records accepted, rejected, and withdrawn outcomes.
work_items.risk: Never turn raw customer data into a fixture without privacy review; reviewer identity and correction text require the same retention/export policy as the trace.

work_items.title: Bridge immutable prompt and evaluator versions to trace and fixture receipts
work_items.why: The Prompt Engine already versions, evaluates, and red-teams patterns; a minimal reference bridge makes production behavior reproducible without moving prompts into a vendor library.
acceptance: A trace stores prompt id, semver, source commit, evaluator id/version, and fixture id as references only.
A promotion receipt resolves those references at the recorded commit and fails closed when a referenced version is absent.
Prompt text, test inputs, and customer corrections are not copied into the trace envelope.
work_items.risk: A reference bridge must not create a second prompt registry or expose private prompt content in operational telemetry.

work_items.title: Make retention, deletion, and approved export lifecycle events replayable
work_items.why: The memory substrate already declares retention policies, but trace and review receipts need the same deletion/export evidence before enterprise claims are credible.
dependencies: Existing SISMemoryRecord retention_policy and provider shadow references
acceptance: Expiry emits a local tombstone/expiry receipt that preserves the minimum non-content provenance needed for audit.
An approved export records recipient adapter, redaction transform, policy decision, and correlation IDs without copying raw payloads.
Deletion and export requests are idempotent and propagate derived-mirror intent; unresolved mirrors remain visible as failed lifecycle receipts.
Tests cover secret local-only behavior, regulated default denial, expiry, and a failed external mirror.
work_items.risk: Tombstones and audit records must not become an undeletable shadow copy of personal or secret content; retention clocks and legal requirements remain tenant policy.

work_items.title: Implement a policy-aware provider gateway adapter
work_items.why: Provides controlled retries, fallbacks, capability routing, and cost/latency receipts without an external gateway becoming mandatory.
acceptance: At least two direct provider adapters share one trace and policy contract.
Fallback is policy-gated and recorded before dispatch.
Retries are limited to classified transient failures, use a declared retry budget/backoff, and record every attempt under one trace.
Non-idempotent tool and approval operations are never automatically retried or replayed; duplicate terminal receipts are rejected.
Optional Orq/OpenTelemetry export is an adapter, not a required path.
work_items.risk: Do not duplicate subscription-capacity planning in request-time routing or let a retry/fallback repeat a charged or irreversible action.

work_items.title: Ship a privacy-safe local operational view
work_items.why: Brings together trace health, blocked actions, evaluation backlog, and capacity without exposing raw private prompts.
acceptance: Shows receipt freshness, outcome state, latency/cost aggregates, policy blocks, and evaluation candidate counts.
Does not render secret payloads.
References canonical artifacts rather than copying their data.
work_items.risk: Do not build a visual dashboard before the receipt contract works.

work_items.title: Enterprise tenancy and vendor adapters
work_items.why: Adds RBAC, SSO/SCIM, quotas, private deployment, and approved enterprise integrations only if a customer needs them.
acceptance: Tenant isolation and audit export are tested.
Vendor exit/export path is exercised.
Commercial margin and operational burden are approved.
work_items.risk: Do not acquire enterprise platform complexity for hypothetical demand.
